stage.arrival: La Rábida. Palos de la Frontera

guideposts.label: Welcome to Huelva
guideposts.detail: Both Cortegana and La Rabida make their debut as La Vuelta stage towns*. The stage is entirely set in the province of Huelva, previously visited by La Vuelta in 1997 and 2022. On the last occasion, stage 17 started from Aracena (km 31.4 on today’s route) and headed to the Monasterio de Tentudia (in the province of Badajoz). guideposts.label: A decisive final week?
guideposts.detail: In the last 25 editions of La Vuelta (2001 - 2025), the overall leader at the beginning of the second week has won the event on 16 occasions. It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year. Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. guideposts.label: Grand Tour success at the eleventh hour?
guideposts.detail: The third week of La Vuelta brings the final six opportunities to take a Grand Tour stage win in 2026. So far, 32 riders from 17 teams and representing 15 nations have won Grand Tour stages this year. The best scorers: 8 stage wins - Tadej Pogacar 5 - Jonas Vingegaard 3 - Matthew Brennan, Paul Magnier, Tim Merlier, Jhonatan Narvaez 2 - Wout van Aert, Richard Carapaz, Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van d

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: Decathlon CMA CGM are strong leaders of the overall team standings with a gap of 57’32’’ to XDS Astana and 1h11’15’’ to Bahrain Victorious.

guideposts.label: 8 riders on the move
guideposts.detail: They've opened a small gap at km 7.

guideposts.label: Back together at km 8
guideposts.detail: The pace is very intense. Riders like Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) said at the start today is likely to be their "last chance" in La Vuelta 26.

guideposts.label: 5 riders on the move
guideposts.detail: As the road rises, a handful of attackers manage to open a small gap. They're at km 14.

guideposts.label: The 5 leaders: Vermaerke, Madouas, Dalby...
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are 15'' ahead of the bunch at km 15.

guideposts.label: 20 kilometres of battle
guideposts.detail: The gap slightly increases: 1'25''.

guideposts.label: 2 minutes
guideposts.detail: At km 28, the peloton trail by 2'14''.

guideposts.label: Meanwhile in the peloton...
guideposts.detail: Jorge Arcas (Movistar) takes care of his leader Enric Mas: “I hope the future will be red. We’ve got six tough days of racing ahead of us. The whole team is fighting tooth and nail alongside Enric and we’re going to try to defend this lead. Today, my job is to support Enric as best I can for as long as possible, making sure he has everything he needs. I’ll make sure he faces as little headwind as

guideposts.label: 48 km covered in the first hour
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) have been racing really hard to open a gap of 2'40''.

guideposts.label: Visma | Lease a Bike control the pace
The two bunches get back together
guideposts.detail: The attackers' lead is back up to 2'20''.

guideposts.label: The situation settles in the bunch
guideposts.detail: And the gap to the breakaway stablises at 2'10''.

guideposts.label: The lowest finish of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: At 8 metres above sea level, the finish in La Rabida is the lowest of La Vuelta 26, slightly below the 10 metres of altitude in Monaco (stage 1), Xeraco (stage 8) and Sevilla (stage 17). On the other hand, Calar Alto (stage 12) was the highest finish of La Vuelta 26, at 2,153 metres of altitude.

guideposts.label: 100 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are still 2 minutes ahead of the bunch.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 45.0 km/h
guideposts.detail: The last gap: 1'30''.

guideposts.label: Timo Roosen withdraws from La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: There are 149 riders still in the race.

guideposts.label: 80 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The gap has slighlty increased again: 1'45''.

guideposts.label: The gap decreases again
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach km 106 with a gap of 1'28''. Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) is setting the pace at the moment.

guideposts.label: 60 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: The peloton trail by 1'05''.

guideposts.label: 40 seconds with 55 km to go
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) face a very hard challenge as they try to hold off the peloton en route to La Rabida.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 3 hours: 45.6 km/h
guideposts.detail: The early attackers have been pushing hard, but the peloton are 39 seconds behind them with 43 km remaining.

guideposts.label: A gap of 25 seconds with 40 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Visma-Lease a Bike, Cofidis and Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe set the pace in the bunch.

guideposts.label: 30 kilometres to go
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) hold to an 18'' gap to the bunch.

guideposts.label: The situation settles ahead of the final rush
guideposts.detail: The peloton are 12'' behind the five leaders with 25 km to go.

guideposts.label: Ivo Oliveira has crashed
guideposts.detail: The Portuguese rider from UAE Emirates XRG is back on his feet but he seems in pain.

guideposts.label: The pace and the tension increase
guideposts.detail: Kevin Vermaerke (UAE Emirates XRG), Valentin Madouas (Groupama-FDJ United), Simon Dalby (Uno-X Mobility), Jasha Sütterlin (Jayco AlUla) and Roland Thalmann (Tudor) are reeled in with 23.5 km to go.

guideposts.label: Flying into the final 20 kilometres
guideposts.detail: A group of stragglers trail by 30 secodns.

guideposts.label: The 6th sprint of La Vuelta 26?
guideposts.detail: Stage 2: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) wins in Manosque Stage 5: Brennan in Roquetes Stage 8: Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) in Xeraco Stage 10: Bastien Tronchon (Groupama-FDJ United) in Elche de la Sierra Stage 11: Brennan in Lorca Stage 16: ?

guideposts.label: Uno-X Mobility pulls the second bunch
guideposts.detail: Magnus Cort was caught behind. But they're getting closer to the first bunch.

guideposts.label: Matthew Brennan wins stages 16 of La Vuelta 26!
guideposts.detail: He becomes the first rider to win four stages in his maiden Grand Tour since Fernando Gaviria in the Giro 2017!

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) 3. Vito Braet (Lotto Intermarché) 4. Jordi Meeus (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) 5. Magnus Cort (Uno-X Mobility)
